summary: Initial integration discovery for inference: Cypher AI evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy and egress, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Agreed next steps to share pricing, SDK samples, and network diagram; plan POC kickoff next week.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
transcript:
15:00:05 Alice Garner: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alice from Redwood, AE on the account. Samir and I will run through integration questions and how teams usually onboard.
15:00:18 Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya here, CTO at Cypher. We'll probably drop in and out — Tom from procurement might have a couple minutes.
15:00:25 Samir Patel: quick intro, I'm Samir on the SE side. We do a lot of integration work with LangChain and LlamaIndex so happy to go deep.
15:00:40 Daniel Park: Hi Daniel, lead ML. main thing for us is low latency for chat use cases and embedding throughput for search. Also want clear SDKs.
15:01:05 Alice Garner: Great. high level — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC or on-prem. We typically triage by SLA/cost/data residency.
15:01:22 Priya Singh: Quick Q — network wise, can Dedicated sit in our VPC? We need peered networking and control over egress.
15:01:35 Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed in a VPC peering model. Our Private option gives you a customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging if you need air-gap. There are a couple of egress patterns — direct peering or through a gateway/proxy.
15:01:58 Maya Chen: When you say gateway/proxy, is that a supported flow? we have strict egress and want all traffic through our gateway so we can apply DLP.
15:02:15 Samir Patel: Totally — customers run a gateway in front of Redwood endpoints or our infra can talk via a NATed egress. We have docs for proxy headers and mutual TLS. I'll send a sample nginx config and our recommended timeout/keepalive settings.
15:02:40 Daniel Park: Great. on SDKs: we use Python + node for our app. What libraries and patterns do you support? is there an official LangChain connector?
15:02:52 Samir Patel: We have official Python and Node SDKs. For LangChain and LlamaIndex, we provide connectors and examples — note: sometimes the package names in examples are slightly different depending on the LangChain version, so we'll send pinned examples. Also show best practices for streaming and function calling.
15:03:20 Maya Chen: Are there prebuilt shims for rate limiting? we have middleware that handles retries and quotas; want to avoid surprise 429s in prod.
15:03:35 Alice Garner: We expose per-key rate limits and per-route quotas — configurable. For Dedicated you can request higher throughput and we provide guidance on token batching to reduce unit cost. We also surface 429s with reason codes so the client can backoff properly.
15:03:58 Tom Reed: From procurement: pricing — how do you bill for Dedicated vs Hosted? and is there a minimum commit?
15:04:12 Alice Garner: Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) — we can share a sizing sheet; there are burst policies. I'll send the spreadsheet after the call.
15:04:33 Priya Singh: Observability: what hooks do we get? We need per-request tracing correlation ids, token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
15:04:47 Samir Patel: Console has per-model dashboards, trace IDs, timing breakdown, and you can forward logs to syslog/CloudWatch/GCS. We also provide request/response hashing options for PII avoidance, and audit logs that meet SOC2 requirements.
15:05:10 Maya Chen: SOC2 is good. we've got an internal control checklist — can you provide a security pack?
15:05:18 Alice Garner: Yes, we'll share redwood-security-pack.pdf which includes SOC2, ISO notes, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration details.
15:05:33 Daniel Park: For the POC we want to run a latency benchmark vs our current setup and test embeddings throughput. What's realistic for setup time?
15:05:45 Samir Patel: For Hosted you can start in hours. For Dedicated it's typically 2-4 weeks to provision depending on region and GPU type; Private is longer. For the POC we usually do Hosted with pinned model and a dedicated route to emulate production. We'll provide a benchmark-sheet.csv with sample load profiles.
15:06:12 Maya Chen: How about model variants — do you support quantized models or custom weights?
15:06:24 Samir Patel: We support various flavors — quantized variants for cost, plus model pinning and rollouts. If you want to bring your own model, that's possible in Private and in some Dedicated cases — we'll need to validate compatibility.
15:06:46 Tom Reed: Legal question: can we limit data retention? we have requirements to purge logs after X days.
15:06:58 Alice Garner: Yes, retention policies are configurable. For enterprise customers we support custom retention windows and are able to purge associated payloads on request; details will be in the security pack and contract addendum.
15:07:18 Priya Singh: A bit more on the gateway — do you support IP allowlisting so we can limit egress to specific endpoints?
15:07:28 Samir Patel: Absolutely, IP allowlisting is supported on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we use regional endpoints and can support customer IP lists for certain tiers. We'll include the IP ranges in the network doc.
15:07:43 Daniel Park: Integration detail: we use LangChain agent + retriever with embeddings restarted every day. Any specific patterns we should follow to keep KV cache warm and minimize cold-start?
15:08:00 Samir Patel: Use prefix caching and keep your KV cache pinned for hot contexts; our runtime supports smart batching and KV cache management. For embeddings, batch requests and warm the cache with a short synthetic run. We'll share code snippets specifically for LangChain retriever hooks.
15:08:28 Maya Chen: Do you have example code for LlamaIndex? We use a forked version which might mismatch.
15:08:38 Samir Patel: We'll send both LangChain and LlamaIndex examples; callout that LlamaIndex compatibility varies by releases — we'll pin versions in the sample repo.
15:08:55 Alice Garner: (slight crosstalk) One more operational Q — how do we monitor cost per team? is there token-level attribution?
15:09:07 Samir Patel: Yes, the console has token-level and route-level cost breakdowns. You can tag requests via metadata to get team-level dashboards. We also provide per-route quotas that can map to teams.
15:09:28 Tom Reed: Procurement: for Dedicated can you do net-30 billing and attach an SLA?
15:09:39 Alice Garner: For enterprise we can do net-30 and SLA add-ons; we'll surface options in the pricing sheet.
15:09:53 Maya Chen: Security follow — KMS integration: do you support customer-managed keys?
15:10:06 Samir Patel: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys for certain plans. Details in security pack.
15:10:25 Daniel Park: Any gotchas with SDK streaming and server-sent events? we've had issues with proxies dropping long-lived connections.
15:10:38 Samir Patel: Good point. We recommend chunked transfer and keepalive tweaks on proxies — we'll include nginx / envoy examples. Also offer a fallback for polling if SSEs are unstable.
15:10:59 Priya Singh: On quotas/rate limits, if we hit a burst, will you automatically route to a cheaper model or is that manual?
15:11:12 Alice Garner: There's a smart routing policy you can enable — automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency vs cost). We can set thresholds and notify on fallbacks.
15:11:28 Maya Chen: For the POC acceptance criteria: target p95 latency < 300ms for single-turn chat and embedding throughput of 200 reqs/s with 512-dim vectors. We should formalize that.
15:11:42 Alice Garner: Noted — we'll include those in the POC plan. Samir will draft the benchmark profile.
15:11:55 Tom Reed: Anything on compliance reviews? we'll need a SOC2 attestation and penetration test reports.
15:12:08 Alice Garner: We'll share SOC2 report and previous pentest summary; for penetration tests we can discuss scoping and NDA.
15:12:20 Daniel Park: If we need custom model ops or tuning, is Redwood providing MLOps support?
15:12:33 Samir Patel: We have an onboarding engineering engagement for Dedicated/Private where we help with model tuning and kernel/quantization recommendations. That can be part of the POC scope.
15:12:50 Maya Chen: Great. any blockers to starting a Hosted POC right away?
15:12:58 Samir Patel: No blockers. We'll provide API keys and a sandbox route. If you want to emulate Dedicated, we'll pin a model and configure rate limits for the POC.
15:13:12 Priya Singh: Send over the IP ranges and the peering checklist.
15:13:20 Alice Garner: Will do.
15:13:26 Alice Garner: Recap: Samir sends SDK examples + benchmark profile; I send pricing/sizing + security pack; Priya provides VPC diagram; Maya confirms POC criteria. We'll tentatively schedule POC kickoff next Monday.
15:13:45 Maya Chen: Sounds good, thanks.
15:13:50 Tom Reed: Thanks everyone.
15:14:00 Alice Garner: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links to the repo and docs.
15:14:05 [meeting ends early at ~14 minutes due to initial sync — extended offline chat on network details]
15:30:00 [offline notes exchanged — not transcribed fully: Priya sent initial network diagram to Alice via email, Samir pushed SDK repo link: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (shared)]
